name: Eicher Motors Ltd
title: Eicher Motors Ltd - 505200 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Royal Enfield Q2 volumes up 15% with dealer stock cut to 7-8 days and capacity lifted to 1.65m/yr, but management says the season was supply-limited and pricing is calibrated, not cost-plus.

triggers.label: Bookings ~21% YTD, backlog unfilled
triggers.quote: we are sitting on quite a substantial booking

guidance.value: 2.45 million units/yr by FY30 (Cheyyar 2m by Q2 FY28; AP 4.5 lakh by 2029-30)

guidance.metric: Dealer inventory reduction via direct billing
guidance.quote: reduce another four, five days of inventory

prior_guidance_check.quote: Post Diwali, our stock is, we are acting, is seven to eight days, including the transit.

red_flags.label: Margin pressure from commodity inflation, only 50% passed on
red_flags.quote: we have done 50% of the commodity impact has covered the increases

red_flags.label: Retail vs registrations gap of ~55,000 units
red_flags.quote: the retails are trailing by 55,000 or so

summary.headline: Eicher Motors Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20% YoY to INR7,422 crore and PAT 15% to INR1,573 crore, with Royal Enfield supply-constrained.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR7,422 crore (up 20% from INR6,172 crore) with EBITDA of INR1,760 crore (vs INR1,512 crore) and PAT of INR1,573 crore (vs INR1,369 crore), including INR186 crore share of VECV profit. Royal Enfield sold a record 376,722 motorcycles (up 15%), with 340,847 in India (up 16%) and 35,875 exports. Management said demand exceeds supply, with bookings about 21% higher year-to-date and dealer stock at 7-8 days including transit, and it is pulling forward Cheyyar capacity to 1.8 million units by Q4 FY27. VECV posted record H1 deliveries of 52,886 vehicles and revenue up 24%.

segments.name: Royal Enfield (motorcycles)
segments.commentary: Record Q2 with 376,722 units (up 15%) and H1 India volume up 23%. Premium 350-650cc mix is about 80-82% of India volume per management. The 440 Himalayan sold out in 17 days and bookings were stopped on day 18 for lack of capacity.

segments.name: VECV (commercial vehicles)
segments.commentary: Q2 sales of 28,071 vehicles (up 28.2%) and H1 of 52,886 (up 21.5%). Revenue INR7,568.6 crore (up 24%), EBITDA margin about 7.8%, PAT INR341.6 crore (up 37%). Volvo Buses delivered a record 422 units in H1. Pro X crossed 5,000 cumulative units, 1,400 of them electric.

segments.name: Flea (electric mobility)
segments.commentary: Flea C6 is now in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and several European cities including London (September). Bookings are slower than inquiries and management says there is no rush to scale.

guidance_outlook: Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu) module 2 to be brought forward to Q4 FY27 from the earlier plan, taking total capacity to about 1.8 million units from 1.65 million, and readily available for Q1 FY28.
Cheyyar module 3 expected in Q2 FY28, taking total capacity to about 2 million units ahead of the 2027 festive season.
Andhra Pradesh plant (216 acres): board approved INR1,225 crore for phase I, adding 0.45 million units; completion expected 2029-2030.
Management does not give forward guidance on volumes or margins; it says the focus is on absolute profit rather than a percentage margin range.
Post-Diwali dealer stock is 7-8 days including transit; the plan is to fill it to about 3-4 weeks and to ramp direct billing to dealers to cut another 4-5 days of stock in C&F agencies.
capex_capacity: Current capacity is about 1.65 million units per year across Vallam and Oragadam plus the Cheyyar first module, after debottlenecking, productivity gains and low-cost automation added about 1.5 million earlier.
Cheyyar brownfield project: investment of INR1,050 crore; module 1 was commissioned in Q2 FY27.
Andhra Pradesh greenfield plant: 216 acres acquired; phase I approved at INR1,225 crore, with 2.5 million total capacity possible after expansion.
Q2 depreciation fell versus Q1 by about INR50 crore because assets tied to the 350cc and 650cc platforms reached end of life; gross block continues to rise.
demand_pricing: Royal Enfield bookings are up about 21% year-to-date, and management says the booking backlog is roughly two months. Inquiries and bookings were still growing about 20% in the most recent period after the festive season.
Dealer stock was 7-8 days including transit in November, versus a normal lean 3-4 weeks; this was an intentional reduction from direct shipments rising to 18% of the period from 1-2%.
Price action: 0.7% hike in October 2026, the fourth hike in the year after 70bps in July and 280bps in January and April. Management says about 50% of the commodity impact has been covered.

Consolidated ASP fell slightly, mainly from geographic mix; standalone ASP rose about 0.5% QoQ on price and variant mix. The 440 and 450 are sold together in the adventure category, with 440 bookings currently paused.

Rural and agricultural states (UP, West Bengal, Bihar, Rajasthan) grew 23% in H1; management says it sees no slowdown from monsoon or rural stress. Exports are growing in Brazil, Colombia, Mexico and the US.

qa_highlights.question: Were retail sales constrained by supply in the season, and what are dealer inventory levels and the capacity bridge to the 2027 season?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply was the constraint; dealer stock was 7-8 days including transit. Capacity is about 1.65 million, rising to 1.8 million by Q4 FY27 and 2 million by Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the magnitude of pending bookings and can ramp-up be accelerated?
qa_highlights.answer: Bookings are up about 20% and the backlog is about two months. Cheyyar module 2 is being pulled forward to January.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Vahan retails about 55,000 below wholesale for April-October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Vahan tallies can include spillovers and it will recheck the numbers. Dealer stock is lean, so retail is expected to match wholesale.

qa_highlights.question: How will electrification affect the premium motorcycle segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called Flea an early-stage, city-focused brand and expects adoption to take 5 years or more. It will avoid a rush and follow the trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand below 350cc or into new segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay in the 250-750cc middle weight range and will not dilute the brand with lower-displacement products.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 440 paused and will it be offered in developing markets?
qa_highlights.answer: The 440 was sold out in 17 days, and bookings were paused on day 18 for lack of capacity. Management is evaluating a 440 for developing markets.

risks_watch: Supply constraints: pending bookings may fall if Cheyyar and the 2027 capacity timelines slip.
Input costs: aluminium and steel moves, and the rupee, against about 50% pass-through so far; further price actions are likely but not guided.
Retail versus wholesale gap: about 55,000 units of Vahan registrations trailing wholesale over April-October; management is reconciling the data.
Demand indicators: inquiries and bookings after festivals; any slowdown in rural demand after monsoon disruption.
Electrification: Flea adoption is slow and the broader EV transition is uncertain. The 440 versus 450 product split is still being evaluated.
VECV market share dipped in some application-oriented segments, per management's answer to a question about share.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, with a record quarter and a strong order backlog. More cautious on forward commitments: management declined to give volume or margin guidance, and it was defensive on the Vahan retail gap and on the impact of commodity costs.
key_quotes: We are not in any tearing rush.

adds.what: Cheyyar module 1 (brownfield, INR1,050 crore Cheyyar project) commissioned in Q2 FY27
Cheyyar module 2 pulled forward to Q4 FY27, taking total capacity from 1.65m to about 1.8m units/yr
Cheyyar module 3 taking total capacity to about 2m units/yr, expected Q2 FY28
Andhra Pradesh plant phase I (216 acres), adding 0.45m units, board approved at INR1,225 crore; completion 2029-30

growth.why: Management gives no formal volume or margin guidance, but demand exceeds supply (bookings up ~21% YTD, ~2-month backlog) and Cheyyar capacity is being added from 1.65m to about 1.8m units by Q4 FY27 and about 2m by Q2 FY28, with Andhra Pradesh phase I (INR1,225 crore, 0.45m units) approved for 2029-30; this is specific but supply-side capacity lands mostly after the next four quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA hit a record INR1,760 crore, but ASP fell slightly on geographic mix and only about 50% of the commodity impact is covered by the 0.7% October hike, so margin gains depend on further pricing and cost actions that management has not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cheyyar module 1 is commissioned, module 2 is under construction for Q4 FY27 (taking capacity from 1.65m to about 1.8m units) and module 3 is planned for Q2 FY28 (about 2m units), with the 1,050 crore Cheyyar project already funded.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Royal Enfield Q2 volume rose 15% to 376,722 units, H1 India volume is up 23%, and bookings are up about 21% YTD with a two-month backlog, but supply is capped at about 1.65m units until Cheyyar module 2 lands.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The INR1,225 crore Andhra Pradesh phase I plant is already board-approved for 0.45m units, with 216 acres acquired and completion in 2029-30; utilisation is effectively at capacity given the 440 sold out in 17 days and bookings were stopped for lack of capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give volume or margin guidance, so there is no formal guide to raise; the stated focus is absolute profit rather than a margin range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The pending-booking backlog depends on Cheyyar module 2 and 3 timelines slipping, and commodity costs are only about 50% passed through, though management gave no formal guidance to cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is evaluating a 440 for developing markets, and the 440 and 450 product split is still under review, but no firm launch date was given.

rows.label: Booking backlog of about two months
rows.why: Bookings are up about 21% YTD with a backlog of roughly two months, and the 440 sold out in 17 days before bookings were stopped on day 18.

rows.label: Dealer stock rebuild and direct billing shift
rows.why: Management plans to lift dealer stock from 7-8 days to 3-4 weeks and cut another 4-5 days of C&F stock by ramping direct billing, which rose from 1-2% to 18% of the period.

rows.label: Further price actions to recover commodity costs
rows.why: Only about 50% of the commodity impact is covered after four hikes in the year (0.7% in October), and further hikes are likely but not guided.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, record quarter and the supply-constrained order book, but cautious on forward commitments and defensive on the Vahan retail-versus-wholesale gap of about 55,000 units and commodity cost pass-through.

quality.why: Consolidated revenue rose 20% to INR7,422 crore, driven mainly by Royal Enfield volume (376,722 units, up 15%, with India up 16%) and VECV volume (Q2 sales up 28.2%), with bookings about 21% higher YTD and a backlog of roughly two months; the brief cites no one-off items in the quarter.
